masteryZone.q: Which of the following schedules of the Indian Constitution lists the names of States and Union Territories along with their territorial extent?
opts: First Schedule
Second Schedule
Third Schedule
Fourth Schedule
masteryZone.sol: The First Schedule contains the names of States and UTs along with their territorial jurisdictions and extents (Articles 1 and 4).

masteryZone.q: Whose emoluments, allowances, and privileges are NOT listed under the Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
opts: President of India
Judges of the Supreme Court
Prime Minister of India
Comptroller and Auditor General
masteryZone.sol: The Prime Minister and other ministers are not listed in the Second Schedule. Their salaries are determined by Parliament under separate laws.

masteryZone.q: The form of oath or affirmation for which of the following is included in the Third Schedule?
opts: President of India
Vice-President of India
Governor of a State
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
masteryZone.sol: The CAG's oath is in the Third Schedule. Oaths for the President (Art. 60), Vice-President (Art. 69), and Governors (Art. 159) are contained in their respective articles, not the 3rd Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following amendments added the Eighth Schedule's 15th language (Sindhi) in 1967?
opts: 21st Amendment Act
71st Amendment Act
92nd Amendment Act
96th Amendment Act
masteryZone.sol: The 21st Amendment Act, 1967, added Sindhi as the 15th language in the Eighth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states is done under the Fourth Schedule. What is the primary basis of this allocation?
opts: Area of the State
Population of the State
Historical treaty with the State
Equal representation for all States
masteryZone.sol: Unlike the United States where all states get equal representation, Rajya Sabha seats are allocated to states based on their population (Fourth Schedule).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following constitutional posts are mentioned in the Second Schedule? (Select all that apply)
opts: President of India
Union Ministers
Judges of High Courts
Speaker of Lok Sabha
masteryZone.sol: The Second Schedule covers the President, Governors, Speaker/Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, Chairman/Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Speaker/Deputy Speaker of State Legislative Assemblies, Chairman/Deputy Chairman of State Legislative Councils, Judges of SC/HC, and CAG. It excludes Ministers.

masteryZone.q: Whose forms of oath/affirmation are included in the Third Schedule? (Select all that apply)
opts: Union Ministers
Members of Parliament
Judges of the Supreme Court
State Governors
masteryZone.sol: The Third Schedule includes oaths for Union/State Ministers, MP/MLA candidates, MPs/MLAs, SC/HC Judges, and CAG. It excludes the President, Vice-President, and Governors.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following languages were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment Act of 2003? (Select all that apply)
opts: Konkani
Bodo
Dogri
Maithili
masteryZone.sol: The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (BDMS) in 2003. Konkani was added by the 71st Amendment in 1992.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following languages were part of the original 14 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule in 1950? (Select all that apply)
opts: Sanskrit
Urdu
Sindhi
English
masteryZone.sol: Sanskrit and Urdu were part of the original 14. Sindhi was added in 1967, and English has never been part of the Eighth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Under the Fourth Schedule, which of the following Union Territories have seats allocated in the Rajya Sabha? (Select all that apply)
opts: Delhi
Puducherry
Chandigarh
Jammu and Kashmir
masteryZone.sol: Only Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir have seats allocated in the Rajya Sabha because they have legislative assemblies. Chandigarh does not.

masteryZone.q: The original Constitution of India adopted in 1949 contained 10 schedules.
masteryZone.sol: False. The original Constitution had 8 schedules. 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th were added later by amendments.

masteryZone.q: The oath of the President of India is administered under the provisions of the Third Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: False. The President's oath is governed by Article 60 of the Constitution, not the Third Schedule.

masteryZone.q: English is recognized as one of the 22 official languages in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: False. English is not listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

masteryZone.q: The salaries and emoluments of High Court Judges are specified in the Second Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: True. High Court Judges are included in Part D of the Second Schedule.

masteryZone.q: The Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the Rajya Sabha based on the territorial size of the States.
masteryZone.sol: False. It allocates seats based on the population of the States.

masteryZone.q: The First Schedule lists the names and extents of the States as well as the Union Territories.
masteryZone.sol: True. It covers both States and UTs (Articles 1 and 4).

masteryZone.q: The Eleventh Schedule (Panchayats) was added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Eleventh Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment, and the Twelfth by the 74th.

masteryZone.q: The form of oath of the Comptroller and Auditor General is included in the Third Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: True. CAG takes oath as per the format in the Third Schedule.

masteryZone.q: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides legislative powers into ______ lists.
masteryZone.sol: It divides powers into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.

masteryZone.q: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the ______ Amendment Act of 1967.
masteryZone.sol: The 21st Constitutional Amendment Act added Sindhi in 1967.

masteryZone.q: The Eleventh Schedule contains ______ functional subjects for Panchayats.
masteryZone.sol: It contains 29 functional subjects (Article 243G).

masteryZone.q: The Twelfth Schedule contains ______ functional subjects for Municipalities.
masteryZone.sol: It contains 18 functional subjects (Article 243W).

masteryZone.q: The spelling 'Oriya' was substituted with 'Odia' in the Eighth Schedule by the ______ Amendment Act, 2011.
masteryZone.sol: The 96th Amendment Act substituted the name/spelling Odia for Oriya.

masteryZone.q: The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution was inserted by the ______ Amendment Act of 1985.
masteryZone.sol: The 52nd Amendment Act added the Tenth Schedule containing anti-defection provisions.

masteryZone.q: Candidates contesting elections to Parliament must take an oath/affirmation according to the ______ Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: Oaths for candidates contesting parliamentary elections are in the Third Schedule.

masteryZone.q: The Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the ______ (Council of States).
masteryZone.sol: The Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the Rajya Sabha.

masteryZone.q: Match the Schedules of the Constitution of India with their core subjects:

options.text: Emoluments and Allowances of constitutional dignitaries
Allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)

masteryZone.sol: Second Schedule: Emoluments; Third Schedule: Oaths; Fourth Schedule: Rajya Sabha seats.

masteryZone.q: Match the Constitutional Amendments with the languages they added to the Eighth Schedule:

options.text: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (added in 2003)

masteryZone.sol: 21st CAA added Sindhi; 71st CAA added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali; 92nd CAA added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali.

masteryZone.q: Match the Schedules with their associated Articles:
masteryZone.sol: First Schedule corresponds to Articles 1 & 4; Fourth Schedule to Articles 4 & 80; Eighth Schedule to Articles 344(1) & 351.

masteryZone.q: What is the decryption of 'S' in the mnemonic 'TEARS OF OLD PM'?
masteryZone.sol: Scheduled Areas (representing the Fifth Schedule).

masteryZone.q: Whose oath is administered under Article 159 of the Indian Constitution instead of the Third Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: The Governor of a State.

masteryZone.q: Which schedule allocates seats in the Rajya Sabha?
masteryZone.sol: The Fourth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: In which year was the Ninth Schedule added to the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: In 1951, by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act.

masteryZone.q: Name the four languages added by the 92nd Amendment Act in 2003.
masteryZone.sol: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (BDMS).

masteryZone.q: Is Rajasthani recognized under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: No, Rajasthani is not recognized in the Eighth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Which amendment added the Twelfth Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

masteryZone.q: Are salaries of members of Parliament (MPs) listed in the Second Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: No, MP salaries are determined by parliamentary laws separately.

opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

masteryZone.q: Why is the oath of the President of India excluded from the Third Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: The President is the supreme constitutional head of the State. A separate Article (Article 60) is dedicated to his oath to reflect the unique dignity, solemnity, and duty of the office (to 'preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution').

masteryZone.q: Why was the Ninth Schedule introduced in the Constitution via the First Amendment in 1951?
masteryZone.sol: It was introduced to protect agrarian reform and Zamindari abolition laws passed by state legislatures from litigation in courts. Landowners were challenging these laws on the ground that they violated the Right to Property (Article 31), which was a Fundamental Right at the time.

masteryZone.q: Why does the Indian Constitution use population rather than equal state representation to allocate Rajya Sabha seats?
masteryZone.sol: The framers chose population-based allocation to ensure democratic proportionality. Equal representation (like in the US Senate) would give disproportionate power to very small states, allowing them to override the legislative will of highly populated states representing a vast majority of the population.

masteryZone.q: How did the Eighth Schedule languages grow from 14 to 22?
masteryZone.sol: They grew through three constitutional amendments: 21st Amendment in 1967 added Sindhi (+1); 71st Amendment in 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali (+3); and the 92nd Amendment in 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (+4).

masteryZone.q: How does the Second Schedule protect the independence of Supreme Court Judges and the CAG?
masteryZone.sol: By listing their emoluments and allowances in the Second Schedule, it provides statutory backing that ensures their salaries cannot be varied or reduced to their disadvantage after appointment, except during a Financial Emergency (Article 360).

masteryZone.q: How does the First Schedule change when a new state is created by Parliament?
masteryZone.sol: When a new state is created (using Article 3 power), Parliament passes an organization act. Under Article 4, this act contains provisions to amend the First and Fourth Schedules to reflect the new state's name, borders, and Rajya Sabha seats without requiring a separate constitutional amendment under Article 368.

masteryZone.q: In 2014, Parliament enacted the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act to carve out the state of Telangana. Analyze how this legislation altered the First and Fourth Schedules.
masteryZone.sol: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended: 1) The First Schedule by adding 'Telangana' as the 29th State and redefining the geographical boundaries of Andhra Pradesh. 2) The Fourth Schedule by reallocating the 18 Rajya Sabha seats of undivided Andhra Pradesh: 11 seats were allocated to Andhra Pradesh and 7 seats were allocated to Telangana.

masteryZone.q: Suppose there is a strong demand for the inclusion of Rajasthani and Bhojpuri in the Eighth Schedule. Evaluate the administrative implications of such an inclusion.
masteryZone.sol: Inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule has major administrative implications: 1) Candidates can write Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) exams in these languages. 2) The Union government is obligated to promote these languages. 3) Bills and documents of national importance must be translated into them. 4) Members of Parliament can speak in these languages with real-time translation.

masteryZone.q: In a state legislature, a MLA is appointed as a Deputy Chief Minister. However, the Third Schedule only mentions 'Minister' and does not contain the word 'Deputy Chief Minister'. Examine the validity of the oath taken by the MLA as Deputy Chief Minister.
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court in Devji v. State (1990) held that the oath is valid. Even though 'Deputy Chief Minister' is a political title not found in the Third Schedule, the person takes the oath of office and secrecy as a 'State Minister'. As long as the core content of the oath matches the minister's format in the Third Schedule, the description 'Deputy Chief Minister' does not invalidate it.

masteryZone.q: Explain the purpose and utility of having 'Schedules' in a written constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Schedules are appendices to the main body of the Constitution. They are used to tabulate long, detailed lists (such as the list of all state names and borders, lists of subjects, list of languages, or forms of oaths) which would otherwise make the constitutional articles extremely cluttered and difficult to read. They separate procedural and descriptive details from the core principles of the articles.

masteryZone.q: Explain the structure of the Third Schedule and point out the notable omissions that commonly trap candidates.
masteryZone.sol: The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations for: 1) Union Ministers 2) Parliamentary candidates 3) Members of Parliament 4) SC Judges 5) CAG 6) State Ministers 7) State Assembly candidates 8) MLAs 9) HC Judges. The key omissions are the President (Art. 60), Vice-President (Art. 69), and State Governors (Art. 159). These dignitaries take oaths according to specific constitutional articles, not the Third Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Provide a brief guide to the history of amendments to the Eighth Schedule and the current status of languages.
masteryZone.sol: Originally, the Eighth Schedule had 14 languages. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi (15th). The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali (16th-18th). The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (19th-22nd). The 96th Amendment (2011) renamed Oriya to Odia. English and Rajasthani are major official languages that are NOT part of the Eighth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, 'Police' is listed under which of the following?
opts: Union List
State List
Concurrent List
Residuary Powers
masteryZone.sol: Police is listed under Entry 2 of the State List (List II). Public Order is Entry 1 of the State List.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following entries falls under the Union List of the Seventh Schedule?
opts: Public Health
Agriculture
Stock Exchanges
Prisons
masteryZone.sol: Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets fall under Entry 48 of the Union List. Public Health, Agriculture, and Prisons are State subjects.

masteryZone.q: In which list of the Seventh Schedule is 'Education' currently placed?
opts: Union List
State List
Concurrent List
It is not in any list
masteryZone.sol: Education is currently placed under Entry 25 of the Concurrent List. It was transferred from the State List by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

masteryZone.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution vests the residuary powers of legislation in the Union Parliament?
opts: Article 245
Article 246
Article 248
Article 254
masteryZone.sol: Article 248 vests the residuary powers of legislation exclusively in the Union Parliament (excluding State Legislatures).

masteryZone.q: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 transferred how many subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List?
opts: 3 subjects
4 subjects
5 subjects
6 subjects
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Amendment transferred 5 subjects: Education, Forests, Weights & Measures, Protection of Wild Animals/Birds, and Administration of Justice.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following subjects are listed in the Union List? (Select all that apply)
opts: Banking
Census
Fisheries
Atomic Energy
masteryZone.sol: Banking (Entry 45), Census (Entry 69), and Atomic Energy (Entry 6) are Union subjects. Fisheries (Entry 21) is a State subject.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following subjects are listed in the State List? (Select all that apply)
opts: Public Order
Prisons
Local Government
Electricity
masteryZone.sol: Public Order (Entry 1), Prisons (Entry 4), and Local Government (Entry 5) are State subjects. Electricity (Entry 38) is in the Concurrent List.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following subjects are in the Concurrent List? (Select all that apply)
opts: Criminal Law
Marriage and Divorce
Forests
Audit of accounts of States
masteryZone.sol: Criminal Law, Marriage and Divorce, and Forests are Concurrent subjects. Audit of State accounts is a Union subject under the control of CAG.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following subjects were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd CAA of 1976? (Select all that apply)
opts: Education
Forests
Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
Sanitation
masteryZone.sol: Education, Forests, and Protection of Wild Animals/Birds were transferred in 1976. Sanitation is part of Public Health and remains a State subject.

masteryZone.q: Under which of the following articles can the Parliament legislate on a State List subject? (Select all that apply)
opts: Article 249
Article 250
Article 252
Article 253
masteryZone.sol: Parliament can legislate on State subjects under Article 249 (national interest), Article 250 (national emergency), Article 252 (consent of two or more states), and Article 253 (international treaties).

masteryZone.q: Agriculture is a subject listed in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: False. Agriculture is in the State List (Entry 14).

masteryZone.q: Residuary powers under the Indian Constitution are vested in the State Legislatures.
masteryZone.sol: False. Article 248 vests residuary powers solely in the Union Parliament.

masteryZone.q: Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) and Civil Procedure Code (CPC) fall under the Concurrent List.
masteryZone.sol: True. Both procedural codes are listed in the Concurrent List (List III).

masteryZone.q: During a National Emergency, Parliament has the power to legislate on any subject in the State List.
masteryZone.sol: True. Article 250 empowers Parliament to legislate on State subjects during an emergency.

masteryZone.q: The number of subjects in the Union List has increased from 97 to 100 since the adoption of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Union List originally had 97 subjects and now has 100.

masteryZone.q: Fisheries is a subject listed under the Union List.
masteryZone.sol: False. Fisheries is a State subject listed under Entry 21 of the State List.

masteryZone.q: Public Order is a State subject separate from Police.
masteryZone.sol: True. Public Order is Entry 1 of List II, while Police is Entry 2 of List II. Both are State subjects.

masteryZone.q: State legislatures cannot make laws on Concurrent List subjects if a parliamentary law already exists.
masteryZone.sol: False. States can make laws on Concurrent subjects, but if they conflict with a central law, the central law prevails, unless the state law received Presidential assent.

masteryZone.q: 'Census' is a subject listed under the ______ List of the Seventh Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: Census is listed under Entry 69 of the Union List (List I).

masteryZone.q: 'Prisons' is a subject listed under the ______ List of the Seventh Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: Prisons is listed under Entry 4 of the State List (List II).

masteryZone.q: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 transferred ______ subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List.
masteryZone.sol: It transferred 5 subjects: Education, Forests, Weights/Measures, Wildlife, and Judicial Administration.

masteryZone.q: Residuary powers of legislation are vested in the Parliament under Article ______ of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Article 248 deals with the residuary legislative powers of Parliament.

masteryZone.q: The Union List currently contains ______ subjects.
masteryZone.sol: The Union List has 100 subjects (originally 97).

masteryZone.q: The State List currently contains ______ subjects.
masteryZone.sol: The State List has 61 subjects (originally 66, reduced due to transfers).

masteryZone.q: The Concurrent List currently contains ______ subjects.
masteryZone.sol: The Concurrent List has 52 subjects (originally 47).

masteryZone.q: Under Article 249, a resolution to legislate on a State subject must be passed by the Rajya Sabha with a ______ majority.
masteryZone.sol: A resolution under Article 249 requires a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

masteryZone.q: Match the subjects with their respective Lists in the Seventh Schedule:
masteryZone.sol: Defence: Union List; Public Health: State List; Forests: Concurrent List.

masteryZone.q: Match the Articles with their constitutional descriptions regarding legislative powers:

options.text: Power of Parliament to legislate in State List in national interest
Legislation for giving effect to international agreements

masteryZone.sol: Article 248: Residuary; Article 249: National Interest; Article 253: International Agreements.

masteryZone.q: Match the subjects of the Seventh Schedule with their entries/placements:
masteryZone.sol: Stock Exchanges: Union List; Local Government: State List; Bankruptcy: Concurrent List.

masteryZone.q: What is the current number of subjects in the State List?
masteryZone.sol: 61 subjects (originally 66).

masteryZone.q: Which list of the Seventh Schedule contains 'Atomic Energy'?
masteryZone.sol: Union List (List I, Entry 6).

masteryZone.q: Under which list of the Seventh Schedule does 'Public Health and Sanitation' fall?
masteryZone.sol: State List (List II, Entry 6).

masteryZone.q: Which amendment act moved 'Forests' and 'Education' from the State List to the Concurrent List?
masteryZone.sol: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

masteryZone.q: Who has the authority to decide if a subject falls under the residuary powers of legislation?
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court and the judiciary, through interpretation.

masteryZone.q: Can a state legislature make a law on a Concurrent subject if a central law already exists?
masteryZone.sol: Yes, but if there is any conflict/repugnancy, the state law becomes void unless it has received the President's assent.

masteryZone.q: Name one Concurrent List subject related to family and civil life.
masteryZone.sol: Marriage and Divorce (or Adoptions, Wills, and Succession).

masteryZone.q: Under which article can Parliament make laws on State subjects to implement international treaties?
masteryZone.sol: Article 253.

masteryZone.q:

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. Since these subjects were not drafted in 1949, they naturally fall under the residuary powers (Article 248).

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Taxes on agricultural income is a subject in the Union List.
Statement II: Fisheries is a subject in the State List.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect because taxes on agricultural income is in the State List (Entry 46). Statement II is correct (Fisheries is Entry 21 of the State List).

masteryZone.q: Why did the 42nd Amendment of 1976 transfer Education and Forests to the Concurrent List?
masteryZone.sol: They were transferred to allow the Union government to formulate national standards, coordinate syllabus reform, implement a uniform forest preservation policy, and manage wildlife across state boundaries effectively. Shifting them to List III allowed both center and states to legislate co-operatively.

masteryZone.q: Why does the Indian Constitution vest residuary powers in the Union Parliament rather than the States?
masteryZone.sol: The framers desired a strong federal center to protect the integrity and unity of India against centrifugal forces. By giving residuary powers to the Union (unlike in the US, where states held residuary powers), they ensured that the national government could address future unforeseen issues (like cybercrime or outer space laws) uniformly.

masteryZone.q: Why does Article 254(2) allow a State law on a Concurrent subject to prevail over a conflicting Central law if it has received Presidential assent?
masteryZone.sol: It is an exception designed to provide regional flexibility. If a State has a unique local context that requires deviation from a central law, it can enact local provisions. By requiring Presidential assent (which means the advice of the Union Cabinet), it ensures that the center retains political supervision over such deviations.

masteryZone.q: How does the Constitution resolve conflicts or overlaps between the Union List and the State List?
masteryZone.sol: Article 246 contains a non-obstante clause, declaring the supremacy of the Union Parliament's power over the State Legislatures' power. In case of overlap, the Union List prevails over both the State List and the Concurrent List.

masteryZone.q: How can Parliament legislate on a State List subject under Article 252?
masteryZone.sol: Two or more States must pass resolutions in their respective assemblies requesting Parliament to legislate on a specific State subject. Parliament can then enact a law. This law applies ONLY to the consenting States, though other States can adopt it later by passing similar resolutions.

masteryZone.q: How did the 42nd Amendment alter the text of the Seventh Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: It did not add new entry numbers. Instead, it omitted five entries from the State List and inserted them as new entries under the Concurrent List. For example, Education was deleted from State List Entry 11 and added to Concurrent List Entry 25, while Forests was added to Concurrent List Entry 17A.

masteryZone.q: The Union Government implements the National Education Policy (NEP), but several States refuse to adopt it, citing state autonomy in education. Examine this dispute in the light of the Concurrent List.
masteryZone.sol: Education is a Concurrent subject (Entry 25 of List III). Thus, both Parliament and State legislatures have power. However, the NEP is a policy framework, not a binding law. If the Union Parliament passes a law on education, it will bind the States. In the absence of a central act, States have the legislative freedom to design their own educational policy. If the State's executive actions conflict with a central act, the central act will prevail under Article 254.

masteryZone.q: The Information Technology Act was enacted in 2000 to regulate e-commerce and cybercrime. Explain which schedule and legislative entry authorized Parliament to pass this law.
masteryZone.sol: Cyber law and electronic commerce did not exist in 1949 and are not listed in any of the three lists of the Seventh Schedule. Therefore, Parliament utilized its **Residuary Powers** under **Article 248** and the Seventh Schedule's implicit residuary entry to enact the IT Act, 2000. It did not require state consent because Article 248 vests exclusive residuary power in Parliament.

masteryZone.q: Examine the conflict between Entry 56 of the Union List (regulation of interstate rivers) and Entry 17 of the State List (water supply, canals, and drainage) during interstate river water disputes.
masteryZone.sol: Entry 17 of the State List gives States power over water supply, irrigation, and canals. However, this is explicitly made 'subject to the provisions of Entry 56 of List I', which gives Parliament power to regulate and develop interstate rivers. In case of disputes (like Cauvery or Sutlej-Yamuna link), Parliament's legislation under Entry 56 (like the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act) overrides state jurisdiction, demonstrating the supremacy of the Union List.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Doctrine of Repugnancy' under Article 254.
masteryZone.sol: The Doctrine of Repugnancy resolves conflicts between Central and State laws on Concurrent List subjects. Under Article 254, if a provision of a state law is repugnant to a central law, the central law prevails, and the state law becomes void to the extent of the repugnancy. An exception exists under Article 254(2) where a state law can prevail in that specific state if it has received Presidential assent, although Parliament can still subsequently amend or repeal it.

masteryZone.q: Explain the 'Doctrine of Pith and Substance' and its application in resolving legislative competence disputes.
masteryZone.sol: The Doctrine of Pith and Substance is used by courts when a law enacted by one legislature (e.g., State) is challenged for encroaching upon the field of another legislature (e.g., Union). 'Pith' means true nature, and 'substance' means essential character. The court looks at the true character of the legislation as a whole, rather than its incidental encroachment on other lists. If the essential subject matter falls within the enacting legislature's list, the law is declared valid.

masteryZone.q: Explain the 'Doctrine of Colorable Legislation' in the context of federal division of powers.
masteryZone.sol: The Doctrine of Colorable Legislation is based on the maxim 'what cannot be done directly, cannot be done indirectly.' It applies when a legislature, lacking the power to make a law on a particular subject, attempts to dress up the law to make it appear within its competence. The court goes behind the form of the law to examine its substance. If the real effect of the law is to legislate on an unauthorized list, the law is struck down as colorable and invalid.

masteryZone.q: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is applicable to the tribal areas of which of the following groups of states?
opts: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Tripura
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, Assam
masteryZone.sol: The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (AMTM) (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)).

masteryZone.q: Under the Fifth Schedule, which authority is empowered to establish a Tribes Advisory Council (TAC)?
opts: President of India
Governor of the State
State Legislature
Union Parliament
masteryZone.sol: The Governor of a State having Scheduled Areas is empowered to establish a Tribes Advisory Council. The President can also direct its setup in states having STs but no Scheduled Areas.

masteryZone.q: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court define the scope of judicial review over the Ninth Schedule?
opts: Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
Kihoto Hollohan Case (1992)
I.R. Coelho Case (2007)
Minerva Mills Case (1980)
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court in I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) ruled on the scope of judicial review over laws in the Ninth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Under the Tenth Schedule, what is the time limit given to a political party to condone a member's unauthorized vote/abstention contrary to the party whip?
opts: 7 days
15 days
30 days
60 days
masteryZone.sol: A member is not disqualified if their political party condones their voting or abstention within 15 days of the occurrence (Paragraph 2(1)(b) of 10th Schedule).

masteryZone.q: To avoid defection disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, what fraction of a legislature party must agree to merge with another political party?
opts: One-third (1/3)
One-half (1/2)
Two-thirds (2/3)
Three-fourths (3/4)
masteryZone.sol: Under the 91st Amendment Act of 2003, at least two-thirds (2/3) of the members of the legislature party must agree to merge to escape defection disqualification.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following states have tribal areas administered under the Sixth Schedule? (Select all that apply)
opts: Assam
Meghalaya
Manipur
Mizoram
masteryZone.sol: Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram are Sixth Schedule states. Manipur is not included in the Sixth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Under the Tenth Schedule, on which of the following grounds can a member of the House be disqualified? (Select all that apply)
opts: Voluntarily giving up membership of the political party
Voting contrary to the direction (whip) issued by the party
An independent member joining any political party after election
A nominated member joining a political party within 6 months of taking office
masteryZone.sol: Voluntarily giving up membership, voting against the whip, and an independent member joining a party are grounds for disqualification. A nominated member is SAFE if they join a party *within* 6 months; they are disqualified only if they join *after* 6 months.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following powers are possessed by Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) under the Sixth Schedule? (Select all that apply)
opts: Power to make laws on land, forests, and canal water
Power to establish village councils and courts for ST disputes
Power to levy taxes on professions, trades, and entry of goods
Power to veto central acts related to atomic energy and defense
masteryZone.sol: ADCs have legislative, judicial, and financial powers (taxation, land laws, village courts). They cannot veto central acts on national subjects like defense or atomic energy.

masteryZone.q: Regarding the decision of the Speaker/Chairman under the Tenth Schedule, which of the following statements are correct? (Select all that apply)
opts: The decision is subject to judicial review on grounds of malafides or natural justice.
Courts can review the decision even before the Speaker makes a final determination.
The Speaker acts as a tribunal when deciding disqualification cases.
The Supreme Court ruled on this in the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992).
masteryZone.sol: The Speaker acts as a tribunal, their decision is subject to judicial review, and this was settled in the Kihoto Hollohan case. However, courts cannot intervene *before* the Speaker's final decision is made.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Fifth Schedule administration? (Select all that apply)
opts: The President has power to declare an area as a Scheduled Area.
A Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) must be established in states with Scheduled Areas.
The Governor can direct that parliamentary laws do not apply to Scheduled Areas.
The TAC has up to 30 members, of which 4 are nominated by the Governor.
masteryZone.sol: President declares scheduled areas, TAC is mandatory in those states, and the Governor can suspend/modify central laws. However, TAC has max 20 members (not 30), and 3/4th are elected ST MLAs, not nominated by the Governor.

masteryZone.q: A nominated member is disqualified if they join a political party within 3 months of taking office.
masteryZone.sol: False. Nominated members are allowed to join a party *within* 6 months; they are disqualified only if they join *after* 6 months.

masteryZone.q: An independent member is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule if they join any political party 1 year after election.
masteryZone.sol: True. Independent members are disqualified if they join a political party at any time after election.

masteryZone.q: Under the Kihoto Hollohan case, the Speaker's decision on defection is completely immune to judicial review.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Supreme Court held that the Speaker's decision is subject to judicial review on grounds of malafides, perversity, or violation of natural justice.

masteryZone.q: Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) under the Sixth Schedule have the power to make laws on canal water and shifting cultivation.
masteryZone.sol: True. ADCs can legislate on land, water courses, shifting cultivation, and social customs, subject to the Governor's assent.

masteryZone.q: The Fifth Schedule administration is currently active in Jammu and Kashmir.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Fifth Schedule applies to 10 states (Andhra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal, Jharkhand, MP, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan).

masteryZone.q: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 abolished the exemption for defection in case of a one-third (1/3) split.
masteryZone.sol: True. The 91st CAA abolished the 1/3rd split protection. Now, only a 2/3rd merger is exempted.

masteryZone.q: All laws placed in the Ninth Schedule are subject to judicial review, regardless of when they were added.
masteryZone.sol: False. Only laws added *after* April 24, 1973 are subject to judicial review under the basic structure test (I.R. Coelho case).

masteryZone.q: The Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) contains a maximum of 30 members.
masteryZone.sol: False. The TAC consists of not more than 20 members (Article 244(1)).

masteryZone.sol: The four states are Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (AMTM).

masteryZone.sol: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 added the Tenth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: Why does the Sixth Schedule provide Autonomous District Councils with legislative and judicial powers, unlike the Fifth Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: Tribal groups in the North-East have historically maintained distinct social, cultural, and self-governing structures, requiring greater local autonomy and legislative safeguards to preserve their lifestyle, whereas 5th Schedule tribes are more integrated into state structures.

masteryZone.q: Why was the split exemption of 1/3rd members deleted from the Tenth Schedule by the 91st Amendment in 2003?
masteryZone.sol: The split provision was being abused for bulk defections. Entire groups of 1/3rd members split from their parent parties to escape disqualification, leading to political instability and horse-trading. Deleting the provision stabilized coalition governments.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Supreme Court in the Kihoto Hollohan case rule that courts cannot intervene before the Speaker makes a final decision on defection?
masteryZone.sol: To prevent parallel proceedings and premature judicial interference in the legislative process. It allows the Speaker to exercise their constitutional power first, while maintaining the court's power of judicial review once a final decision has been made.

masteryZone.q: How does a Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Council raise revenue for its functioning?
masteryZone.sol: ADCs are empowered to assess and collect land revenue, impose taxes on professions, trades, callings, animals, vehicles, and levy tolls on passengers/goods entering the district. They also receive shares of royalties from licensing mineral prospecting in their areas.

masteryZone.q: How can a law in the Ninth Schedule be declared unconstitutional after the I.R. Coelho case?
masteryZone.sol: The petitioner must prove that: 1) The law was inserted in the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973. 2) The law violates Fundamental Rights (Articles 14, 19, or 21). 3) In doing so, it damages or destroys the Basic Structure of the Constitution. If both criteria are met, the court can strike down the law.

masteryZone.q: How are dispute resolutions handled within Sixth Schedule tribal areas?
masteryZone.sol: ADCs can establish village councils or district courts to try suits and cases between Scheduled Tribe members. They can appoint officers to preside over these courts. High Court jurisdiction over these courts is specified and regulated by the Governor.

masteryZone.q: In the Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) case, the Supreme Court delivered a landmark ruling regarding tribal lands in Fifth Schedule areas. Analyze the key constitutional outcome of this judgment.
masteryZone.sol: In the Samatha case, the Supreme Court held that the word 'person' in the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation includes the State Government. Consequently, the state government cannot lease out tribal lands in Scheduled Areas to private mining companies or non-tribals for industrial activities. All such leases were declared null and void. The court ruled that only state-owned corporations or cooperative societies of tribal people could undertake mining in these areas, thereby safeguarding tribal land and livelihood under the Fifth Schedule.

masteryZone.q: A nominated member of Rajya Sabha joins a political party 7 months after taking his oath. The opposition party demands his disqualification, while the member argues he was unaware of the rules. Evaluate the validity of this disqualification demand under the Tenth Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: The disqualification demand is valid. Under Paragraph 2(3) of the Tenth Schedule, a nominated member of a House becomes disqualified if they join a political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which they take their seat. Since the member joined the party 7 months (which is after the 6-month grace period) after taking office, they have violated the Tenth Schedule, and the plea of ignorance of rules is not legally acceptable. The Speaker/Chairman must disqualify the member.

masteryZone.q: Examine the status of a member who has been expelled from their political party. If such an expelled member votes against the party whip in the House, can they be disqualified under the Tenth Schedule?
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court in G. Viswanathan v. Speaker (1996) held that an expelled member continues to belong to the political party that set them up as a candidate for the election, unless they join another party or sit as an independent. For the purpose of the Tenth Schedule, they are still subject to the party whip. If they vote against the whip, they can be disqualified under the Tenth Schedule. Expulsion from the party does not automatically shield a legislator from anti-defection laws inside the House.

masteryZone.q: Explain the constitutional safeguards provided under the Sixth Schedule for Autonomous Districts and Regional Councils.
masteryZone.sol: The Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)) establishes Autonomous Districts and Regional Councils. Key safeguards include: 1) Legislative power to make laws on land, forests, water, village administration, and inheritance (subject to Governor's assent). 2) Judicial power to constitute village councils and courts to resolve disputes between Scheduled Tribe members. 3) Financial power to levy taxes and royalties. 4) Exclusion/modification of Parliament or State Legislature acts unless specifically directed by the Governor/President.

masteryZone.q: Explain the mechanism and significance of the 'Tribes Advisory Council' (TAC) under the Fifth Schedule.
masteryZone.sol: Under the Fifth Schedule, a Tribes Advisory Council must be established in states with Scheduled Areas (and states with STs if directed by the President). It consists of not more than 20 members, where three-fourths (3/4) must be representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assembly. Its role is to advise the Governor on matters pertaining to the welfare and advancement of the Scheduled Tribes in the state. The Governor refers matters to the TAC before enacting regulations for Scheduled Areas.

masteryZone.q: Explain the evolution of the Ninth Schedule from its inception to the basic structure test.
masteryZone.sol: The Ninth Schedule was inserted by the 1st Amendment in 1951 along with Article 31B to protect agrarian land reforms from being struck down under the Right to Property (Article 31). Initially, it provided complete immunity from judicial review. However, in the I.R. Coelho case (2007), the Supreme Court ruled that there is no absolute immunity. Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973 (the date of Kesavananda Bharati judgment) are subject to judicial review and can be struck down if they violate fundamental rights and destroy the basic structure of the Constitution.
